    62	  // ==== heap allocation (constructed lists become objects) ==================
    63	  // Cons-form emission with a freshness guard (the heap-list-probe discipline:
    64	  // an update-form H[N <- _] never re-normalizes symbolically). heapLoc is
    65	  // monotonic — it does NOT wind back at #pop: returned lists escape by ref.
    66	  // A bare list(VS) Val stays legal (read-only inputs in claims flow unboxed);
    67	  // only CONSTRUCTORS in program syntax allocate.
    68	  syntax Bool ::= isRefV(Val) [function, total]
    69	  rule isRefV(ref(_:Int)) => true
    70	  rule isRefV(_:Val)      => false [owise]
    71	
    72	  // closure cells (Python-faithful capture): the heap holds cellV(V); a
    73	  // cellRef surfacing as the k-redex reads through (lookup is the only use —
    74	  // cellRefs never escape to user-visible values)
    75	  syntax HeapVal ::= cellV(Val)
    76	  syntax Bool ::= isCellRef(Val) [function, total]
    77	  rule isCellRef(cellRef(_:Int)) => true
    78	  rule isCellRef(_:Val)          => false [owise]
    79	  // k-top deref for cell-bound reads surfacing INSIDE the annotated frame
    80	  // (AugAssign's in-place read and friends). The "$cells" guard keeps this
    81	  // DECIDABLY inapplicable in plain frames — an unguarded rule lets the
    82	  // prover narrow abstract k-top values into cellRef junk (probed on
    83	  // 26-remove-duplicates). Cross-frame reads (a comprehension closure
    84	  // reading the enclosing function's cellvar) deref inside #look instead.
    85	  rule <k> cellRef(H:Int) => V ... </k>
    86	       <env> L:Int </env>
    87	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    88	       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(V:Val) ... </heap>
    89	       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
    90	       [priority(40)]
    91	
    92	  // write through a cell (Assign / #bindP / #bindTgt dispatch here on
    93	  // cell-bound names)
    94	  // a keyword argument cools to a TAGGED value (consumed by kw-aware builtins)
    95	  syntax Val ::= kwV(String, Val)
    96	  syntax KItem ::= #kwTag(String)
    97	  rule <k> KwArg(N:String, E:Expr) => E ~> #kwTag(N) ... </k>
    98	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #kwTag(N:String) => kwV(N, V) ... </k>
    99	       requires notBool isKwV(V)
   100	  syntax Bool ::= isKwV(Val) [function, total]
   101	  rule isKwV(kwV(_:String, _:Val)) => true
   102	  rule isKwV(_:Val)                => false [owise]
   103	
   104	  // the frame marker carries the CONCRETE cellvar list, so cell-write dispatch
   105	  // decides by pnMember even over an abstract frame rest (no prover branching)
   106	  syntax Val ::= cellsMark(ParamNames)
   107	  syntax ParamNames ::= cellsOf(Val) [function]
   108	  rule cellsOf(cellsMark(CVS:ParamNames)) => CVS
   109	  syntax Bool ::= pnMember(String, ParamNames) [function, total]
   110	  rule pnMember(_:String, .ParamNames) => false
   111	  rule pnMember(X:String, (P:String, R:ParamNames)) => X ==String P orBool pnMember(X, R)
   112	
   113	  syntax KItem ::= #cellW(Val, Val)
   114	  rule <k> #cellW(cellRef(H:Int), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
   115	       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(_:Val => V) ... </heap>
   116	
   117	  syntax KItem ::= #alloc(Val)
   118	  rule <k> #alloc(V:Val) => ref(N) ... </k>
   119	       <heap>    H:Map => (N |-> V) H </heap>
   120	       <heapLoc> N:Int => N +Int 1 </heapLoc>
   121	       requires notBool N in_keys(H)
   122	
   123	  // ==== module load + statement sequencing ==================================
   124	  syntax KItem ::= #loadAll(Module)
   125	  rule <k> #loadAll(Module(SS:Stmts)) => SS ... </k>
   126	  rule <k> (S:Stmt SS:Stmts):Stmts => S ~> SS ... </k>
   127	  rule <k> .Stmts => .K ... </k>
   128	
   129	  // ==== Name lookup (walk the scope chain; builtins live in the -1 scope) ====
   130	  syntax KItem ::= #look(String, Int)
   131	  rule <k> Name(X:String) => #look(X, L) ... </k> <env> L:Int </env>
   132	  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => {M[X]}:>Val ... </k>
   133	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
   134	       requires X in_keys(M)
   135	  // a SYNTACTICALLY cell-bound name reads through the heap cell AT THE
   136	  // LOOKUP (higher priority beats the plain return above on concrete cell
   137	  // bindings; abstract claim values take the plain rule unchanged) — this
   138	  // covers cross-frame cell reads (a comprehension closure reading the
   139	  // enclosing function's cellvar) without a narrowing-prone k-top redex
   140	  // guarded on the FOUND frame's DECLARED cellvars (pnMember over the
   141	  // cellsMark): decidable for every concrete frame pin — plain frames and
   142	  // non-cell names prune outright, so an abstract looked-up value never
   143	  // drags a narrowing cellV heap match along (probed on 5-intersperse and
   144	  // Q4's abstract `numbers` in the annotated frame)
   145	  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => V ... </k>
   146	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
   147	       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(V:Val) ... </heap>
   148	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool "$cells" in_keys(M)
   149	        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
   150	        andBool {M[X]}:>Val ==K cellRef(H)
   151	       [priority(40)]
   152	  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => #look(X, P) ... </k>
   153	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, parent(P:Int)) ... </scopes>
   154	       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))
   155	
   156	  // the ONE predefined builtins scope (the -1 frame; claims write `-1 |-> builtinsScope`)
   157	  syntax Scope ::= "builtinsScope" [function, total]
   158	  rule builtinsScope
   159	    => scope(.Map [ "len"    <- builtinV("len")    ]
   160	                  [ "set"    <- builtinV("set")    ]
   161	                  [ "sum"    <- builtinV("sum")    ]
   162	                  [ "abs"    <- builtinV("abs")    ]
   163	                  [ "min"    <- builtinV("min")    ]
   164	                  [ "max"    <- builtinV("max")    ]
   165	                  [ "ord"    <- builtinV("ord")    ]
   166	                  [ "chr"    <- builtinV("chr")    ]
   167	                  [ "range"  <- builtinV("range")  ]
   168	                  [ "all"    <- builtinV("all")    ]
   169	                  [ "any"    <- builtinV("any")    ]
   170	                  [ "zip"    <- builtinV("zip")    ]
   171	                  [ "isinstance" <- builtinV("isinstance") ]
   172	                  [ "sorted" <- builtinV("sorted") ]
   173	                  [ "list"   <- builtinV("list")   ]
   174	                  [ "round"  <- builtinV("round")  ]
   175	                  [ "bin"    <- builtinV("bin")    ]
   176	                  [ "enumerate" <- builtinV("enumerate") ]
   177	                  [ "map"    <- builtinV("map")    ]
   178	                  [ "eval"   <- builtinV("eval")   ]
   179	                  [ "int"    <- typeV("int")       ]
   180	                  [ "str"    <- typeV("str")       ]
   181	                  [ "float"  <- typeV("float")     ], root)
   182	
   183	  // ==== argument/element evaluation: ONE left-to-right loop, tagged by destination ==
   184	  // (list/tuple literals and calls all use it; modules extend ApplyK with their tags)
   185	  syntax ApplyK ::= toCall(Val)
   186	  syntax KItem  ::= #evalArgs(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
   187	                  | #evalArgCont(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
   188	                  | #applyK(ApplyK, Vals)
   189	  rule <k> #evalArgs((A:Expr, REST:Exprs), ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => A ~> #evalArgCont(REST, ACC, K) ... </k>
   190	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #evalArgCont(REST:Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #evalArgs(REST, appendVal(ACC, V), K) ... </k>
   191	  rule <k> #evalArgs(.Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #applyK(K, ACC) ... </k>
   192	
   193	  // ==== Int / Bool / None literals ==========================================
   194	  rule <k> Int(I:Int)   => I ... </k>
   195	  rule <k> Bool(B:Bool) => B ... </k>
   196	  rule <k> NoneVal      => noneV ... </k>
   197	
   198	  // ==== truthy (If, Assert, BoolOp, IfExp, not, While) ======================
   199	  syntax Bool ::= truthy(Val) [function]
   200	  rule truthy(B:Bool)          => B
   201	  rule truthy(noneV)           => false
   202	  rule truthy(I:Int)           => I =/=Int 0
   203	  rule truthy(str(S:IntSeq))   => notBool (S ==K .IntSeq)
   204	  rule truthy(list(V:ValSeq))  => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
   205	  rule truthy(tuple(V:ValSeq)) => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
   206	
   207	  // ==== extensible operator dispatch (cases added by the construct modules) ==
   208	  syntax Val  ::= applyUn(String, Val) [function]
   209	  syntax Val  ::= applyBin(String, Val, Val) [function]
   210	  syntax Bool ::= applyCmp(String, Val, Val) [function]
   211	
   212	  // ==== shared list helpers =================================================
   213	  syntax Vals ::= appendVal(Vals, Val) [function, total]
   214	  rule appendVal(.Vals, V:Val)              => V , .Vals
   215	  rule appendVal((V0:Val, VS:Vals), V:Val)  => V0 , appendVal(VS, V)
   216	
   217	  syntax ValSeq ::= vals2valSeq(Vals) [function, total]
   218	  rule vals2valSeq(.Vals)            => .ValSeq
   219	  rule vals2valSeq((V:Val, VS:Vals)) => vCons(V, vals2valSeq(VS))
   220	
   221	  // ==== shared sequence length (len / summaries across many modules) ========
   222	  // (positional access valSeqAt/intSeqAt + normIdx live in subscript.k)
   223	  syntax Int ::= vsLen(ValSeq) [function, total]
   224	  rule vsLen(.ValSeq)                => 0
   225	  rule vsLen(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq)) => 1 +Int vsLen(S)
   226	
   227	  syntax Int ::= isLen(IntSeq) [function, total]
   228	  rule isLen(.IntSeq)                => 0
   229	  rule isLen(iCons(_:Int, S:IntSeq)) => 1 +Int isLen(S)
   230	
   231	  // in-bounds positional write (list subscript-assign); OOB leaves the seq unchanged
   232	  // (valid programs write in-bounds — mirrors valSeqAt's total-but-underspecified stance)
   233	  syntax ValSeq ::= setVSAt(ValSeq, Int, Val) [function, total]
   234	  rule setVSAt(.ValSeq, _:Int, _:Val)               => .ValSeq
   235	  rule setVSAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), 0, V:Val)    => vCons(V, S)
   236	  rule setVSAt(vCons(W:Val, S:ValSeq), I:Int, V:Val) => vCons(W, setVSAt(S, I -Int 1, V))
   237	       requires I >Int 0
   238	  rule setVSAt(VS:ValSeq, I:Int, _:Val)             => VS
   239	       requires I <Int 0
   240	endmodule

     2	// ONE call route for every callable: evaluate the callee to a VALUE (name lookup reaches
     3	// builtins at the root; a cooled Attribute is a bound method), evaluate the args (the shared
     4	// #evalArgs loop in core.k), then dispatch on the callee value:

    10	module MPY-CALL

    12	  imports MPY-BUILTINS
    13	  imports MPY-FUNCTIONS
    14	
    15	  // a cooled attribute is a bound method value

    17	
    18	  // evaluate callee, then args ([owise]: problem-local Call interceptions beat this)

    23	  // ==== dispatch on the callee value ========================================
    24	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyMethod(OBJ, M, ACC) ... </k>
    25	
    26	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sum")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #sumAcc(OBJ, 0) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("all")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #allAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("any")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #anyAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    29	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("max")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #maxAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> #apply…997 tokens truncated…Ref(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
    92	       <heap>    H:Map => (N |-> cellV(noneV)) H </heap>

     1	// reference/src/semantics/controls.k — MPY-CONTROLS
     2	
     3	module MPY-CONTROLS
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-TUPLE
     6	  imports MPY-ITER
     7	
     8	  // ==== Assign / AugAssign (write the current scope; RHS evaluated by strictness) ==
     9	  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
    10	       <env> L:Int </env>
    11	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
    12	  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => #cellW({M[X]}:>Val, V) ... </k>
    13	       <env> L:Int </env>
    14	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    15	       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
    16	        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
    17	        andBool X in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[X]}:>Val)
    18	       [priority(40)]
    19	
    20	  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => .K ... </k>
    21	       <env> L:Int </env>
    22	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- applyBin(OP, {M[X]}:>Val, V) ], _) ... </scopes>
    23	       requires X in_keys(M)
    24	  // `lst += [..]` where lst is a heap ref: the generic rule leaves applyBin(OP, ref, V) — but the
    25	  // ref-deref preemption is BinOp-level (operators.k), so applyBin never derefs and it sticks. Route
    26	  // the ref case through BinOp so the deref + list-concat + #alloc path fires (result is a fresh ref).
    27	  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => Assign(Name(X), BinOp(OP, Name(X), V)) ... </k>
    28	       <env> L:Int </env>
    29	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    30	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    31	       [priority(40)]
    32	
    33	  // ==== import trivia: `from math import floor, ceil` binds the supported
    34	  // names as builtins in the current scope; every other import is a no-op
    35	  rule <k> ImportFrom("math", NS:ParamNames) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> ImportFrom(_:String, _:ParamNames) => .K ... </k> [owise]
    37	  syntax KItem ::= #bindImports(ParamNames)
    38	  rule <k> #bindImports(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
    39	  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    40	       <env> L:Int </env>
    41	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ N <- builtinV(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
    42	       requires N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil"
    43	  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    44	       requires notBool (N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil")
    45	
    46	  // ==== Expr statement: evaluate for effect, discard the value ===============
    47	  // (bare calls — mutator methods, docstrings; the WP0 statement-trivia rung)
    48	  rule <k> Expr(_:Val) => .K ... </k>
    49	
    50	  // ==== If (condition evaluated by strictness) ==============================
    51	  syntax KItem ::= #branch(Bool, Stmts, Stmts)
    52	  rule <k> If(C:Val, T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => #branch(truthy(C), T, E) ... </k>
    53	  rule <k> #branch(true,  T:Stmts, _:Stmts) => T ... </k>
    54	  rule <k> #branch(false, _:Stmts, E:Stmts) => E ... </k>
    55	
    56	  // ==== IfExp: ternary T if C else E ========================================
    57	  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, T:Expr, _:Expr) => T ... </k>
    58	       requires truthy(V)
    59	  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, _:Expr, E:Expr) => E ... </k>
    60	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    61	
    62	  // ==== For: one loop, in-cell continuation, over #iterNext =================
    63	  // (the iterable is evaluated once, by strictness; the protocol stays rewrites —
    64	  // circularities anchor on #loop and narrowing substitutes the structure)
    65	  syntax KItem ::= #loop(Val, Expr, Stmts) | #loopStep(Expr, Stmts)
    66	                 | #while(Expr, Stmts) | #whileCond(Expr, Stmts)
    67	                 | #loopLbl(K) | "#cont" | "#brk"
    68	
    69	  rule <k> For(T:Expr, OBJ:Val, B:Stmts) => #loop(OBJ, T, B) ... </k>
    70	
    71	  rule <k> #loop(IT:Iterable, T:Expr, B:Stmts) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #loopStep(T, B) ... </k>
    72	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #loopStep(_:Expr, _:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    73	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, REST:Iterable) ~> #loopStep(T:Expr, B:Stmts)
    74	        => #bindTgt(T, V) ~> B ~> #loopLbl(#loop(REST, T, B)) ... </k>
    75	
    76	  // ==== While ==============================================================
    77	  rule <k> While(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => #while(C, B) ... </k>
    78	  rule <k> #while(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => C ~> #whileCond(C, B) ... </k>
    79	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #whileCond(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => B ~> #loopLbl(#while(C, B)) ... </k>
    80	       requires truthy(V)
    81	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #whileCond(_C:Expr, _B:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    82	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    83	
    84	  // ==== loop control (break / continue) =====================================
    85	  rule <k> #loopLbl(NEXT:K) => NEXT ... </k>
    86	  rule <k> Continue => #cont ... </k>
    87	  rule <k> Break => #brk ... </k>
    88	  rule <k> #cont ~> #loopLbl(NEXT:K) => NEXT ... </k>
    89	  rule <k> #cont ~> (_:KItem => .K) ... </k> [owise]
    90	  rule <k> #brk ~> #loopLbl(_:K) => .K ... </k>
    91	  rule <k> #brk ~> (_:KItem => .K) ... </k> [owise]
    92	
    93	  // ==== heap-object deref at the truthiness/iteration consumers ==============
    94	  // (priority(40) preempts the generic Val rules so truthy/#loop never see a ref)
    95	  rule <k> If(ref(H:Int), T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => If(V, T, E) ... </k>
    96	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    97	       [priority(40)]
    98	  rule <k> IfExp(ref(H:Int), T:Expr, E:Expr) => IfExp(V, T, E) ... </k>
    99	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   100	       [priority(40)]
   101	  rule <k> ref(H:Int) ~> #whileCond(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => V ~> #whileCond(C, B) ... </k>
   102	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   103	       [priority(40)]
   104	  // For derefs its iterable ONCE at loop start (iteration is over the snapshot;
   105	  // mutating the iterated list inside its own loop is outside the subset)
   106	  rule <k> For(T:Expr, ref(H:Int), B:Stmts) => For(T, V, B) ... </k>
   107	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   108	       [priority(40)]
   109	endmodule

     3	module MPY-LIST
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	  imports MPY-OPERATORS
     7	
     8	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's list case) =======================
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(.ValSeq))                => #iterDone ... </k>
    10	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))) => #iterYield(V, list(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== ListExpr: [...] literal -> a fresh heap object =======================
    13	  syntax ApplyK ::= "toList"
    14	  rule <k> ListExpr(ES:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ES, .Vals, toList) ... </k>
    15	  rule <k> #applyK(toList, ACC:Vals) => #alloc(list(vals2valSeq(ACC))) ... </k>
    16	
    17	  // ==== list ops: + / == / != ===============================================
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= valSeqConcat(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    19	  rule valSeqConcat(.ValSeq, T:ValSeq)                => T
    20	  rule valSeqConcat(vCons(V:Val, S:ValSeq), T:ValSeq) => vCons(V, valSeqConcat(S, T))
    21	
    22	  // list + list constructs a NEW object (k-cell — it allocates; operands land here
    23	  // already deref'd). priority(45) beats the generic BinOp dispatch.
    24	  rule <k> BinOp("+", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => #alloc(list(valSeqConcat(A, B))) ... </k>

module AUDIT-BRIDGE-FREE-VERIFICATION

  rule auditAllInts(.ValSeq) => true

    requires I <Int 0
  rule auditMagnitudeAcc(vCons(I:Int, VS:ValSeq), A:Int)
    => auditMagnitudeAcc(VS, A +Int I)
    requires I >=Int 0

  syntax Int ::= auditSignAcc(ValSeq, Int) [function]

  rule auditSignAcc(vCons(I:Int, VS:ValSeq), S:Int)
    => auditSignAcc(VS, 0 -Int S)

  rule auditSignAcc(vCons(0, VS:ValSeq), _S:Int)
    => auditSignAcc(VS, 0)
  rule auditSignAcc(vCons(I:Int, VS:ValSeq), S:Int)
    => auditSignAcc(VS, S)
    requires I >Int 0

  rule auditLastInt(vCons(I:Int, .ValSeq)) => I

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build a line-addressable inventory of K declarations and rules."""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
import re
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path


SCRATCH = Path("/tmp/audit-work/128-prod-signs.HMXf22")
EVIDENCE = Path("/audit-output/evidence")
START = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(requires|module|imports|configuration|syntax|context|rule|claim)\b"
)
ATTR = re.compile(
    r"\b(functional|function|total|simplification|concrete|"
    r"priority|owise|macro-rec|macro|strict|seqstrict|symbol|opaque)\b"
)


def chunks(path: Path):
    lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    current = None
    for number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        match = START.match(line)
        if match:
            if current is not None:
                yield current
            current = {
                "file": str(path.relative_to(SCRATCH)),
                "line": number,
                "kind": match.group(1),
                "lines": [line],
            }
        elif current is not None:
            stripped = line.strip()
            if stripped == "endmodule":
                yield current
                current = None
            else:
                current["lines"].append(line)
    if current is not None:
        yield current


def main() -> int:
    paths = [SCRATCH / "reference-semantics" / "semantics.k"]
    paths.extend(
        sorted((SCRATCH / "reference-semantics" / "semantics").glob("*.k"))
    )
    paths.append(SCRATCH / "verification.k")
    records = []
    for path in paths:
        for chunk in chunks(path):
            text = " ".join(part.strip() for part in chunk.pop("lines") if part.strip())
            attrs = sorted(set(ATTR.findall(text)))
            source_class = (
                "candidate-proof-extension"
                if chunk["file"] == "verification.k"
                else "trusted-supplied-semantics"
            )
            records.append(
                {
                    **chunk,
                    "source_class": source_class,
                    "attributes": ",".join(attrs),
                    "text": text,
                }
            )

    with (EVIDENCE / "rule-inventory.tsv").open(
        "w", encoding="utf-8", newline=""
    ) as output:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(
            output,
            fieldnames=[
                "file",
                "line",
                "kind",
                "source_class",
                "attributes",
                "text",
            ],
            delimiter="\t",
        )
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(records)

    by_source = Counter(record["source_class"] for record in records)
    by_attribute = Counter()
    for record in records:

            item for item in record["attributes"].split(",") if item

    summary = {
        "files": len(paths),
        "records": len(records),
        "by_kind": dict(sorted(by_kind.items())),
        "by_source_class": dict(sorted(by_source.items())),

*** Add File: REVIEW.md
+# Independent adversarial audit: 128-prod-signs
+
+## Executive decision
+
+The candidate reconstructs to `#Top`, the submitted Python program matches the
+trusted canonical implementation on extensive finite testing, and the claims
+are result-constraining. It is nevertheless **not a legitimate proof** under
+the supplied semantics.
+
+The decisive defect is the priority-40 loop rule at
+`/candidate/verification.k:74`. It is an operational bridge whose match domain
+is broader than the fixed-semantics transition it claims to replace. On the
+valid integer list `[5]`, in a well-formed frame where the loop target `value`
+is a closure cell, the rule concludes that the scope binding becomes the
+integer `5` while the heap cell remains `99`. Fixed semantics instead preserves
+the `cellRef(0)` binding and updates heap cell 0 to `5`.
+
+This is a machine-checked false-conclusion witness:
+
+- With the candidate bridge, the false transition proves `#Top`, exit 0:
+  [cell-witness-bridge-spec.k](evidence/cell-witness-bridge-spec.k) and
+  [cell-witness-bridge.log](evidence/cell-witness-bridge.log).
+- With the bridge removed and only supplied semantics present, the identical
+  claimed transition is rejected, exit 1. The residual displays the actual
+  fixed result—`"value" |-> cellRef(0)` and `0 |-> cellV(5)`:
+  [cell-witness-fixed-spec.k](evidence/cell-witness-fixed-spec.k) and
+  [cell-witness-fixed.log](evidence/cell-witness-fixed.log).
+
+The submitted function itself reaches a plain, non-cell frame, but that does
+not validate a globally false ordinary rewrite. The Kit extension-soundness
+contract specifically requires equivalence over the bridge's complete match
+domain; an off-path false rule must be narrowed before its `#Top` can be used.
+
+All audit execution occurred in
+`/tmp/audit-work/128-prod-signs.HMXf22`. Nothing from a
+candidate-provided compiled definition or cache was copied or reused.
+
+## 1. Input and provenance integrity
+
+The rendered mode and trusted mounts are consistent:
+`SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS` was requested and
+`/reference/reference-semantics` is present. There is no infrastructure breach.
+
+The recursive, no-dereference comparison of
+`/candidate/reference-semantics` against the trusted tree returned exit 0.
+There are no symlinks in either semantics tree and no missing, added, or
+changed entries. Candidate `prompt.py` and `py2mpy.py` are byte-identical to
+their trusted mounted versions. `solution.py`, `solution.mpy`, `spec.k`, and
+`verification.k` are regular files, not symlinks.
+
+Four requested generation-provenance artifacts are absent:
+
+- `/candidate/run-input.json`
+- `/candidate/metrics.json`
+- `/candidate/codex-last.txt`
+- `/candidate/codex-output.log`
+
+No structured generation trace was present at candidate top level. These
+omissions limit provenance review but are not an infrastructure contradiction.
+The complete checks, source SHA-256 values, command, and status are in
+[stage1_integrity.sh](evidence/stage1_integrity.sh) and
+[stage1-integrity.log](evidence/stage1-integrity.log).
+
+## 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks
+
+The trusted contract says: for a nonempty integer array, add the magnitudes of
+all elements and multiply that sum by the product of their signs, where each
+sign is `-1`, `0`, or `1`; return `None` for the empty array.
+
+The trusted canonical function computes the same value using `abs`, negative
+parity, and a zero-membership test. Candidate `solution.py` uses a single loop:
+negative elements add `-value` and flip `sign`; nonnegative elements add
+`value`, with zero setting `sign` to zero. The branches cover all Python
+integers and preserve the contract.
+
+The submitted `solution.mpy` was independently regenerated using
+`/reference/py2mpy.py`. `cmp` returned exit 0, establishing byte identity; see
+[translate.log](evidence/translate.log).
+
+The independent differential test imported the trusted canonical entry point
+and the scratch copy of the candidate entry point. Its scope was:
+
+- 16 named documented, empty, branch-boundary, large-integer, and long-list
+  cases;
+- every array of lengths 0 through 5 over integers `[-3,3]`—19,608 cases;
+- 1,000 seeded generated arrays of lengths 0 through 20 and values in
+  `[-1,000,000,1,000,000]`.
+
+All 20,624 cases also went through a separately written contract oracle.
+There were zero result mismatches and zero input mutations. The exact script,
+all JSONL inputs, empty mismatch file, summary, and command/status are
+[differential_test.py](evidence/differential_test.py),
+[differential-inputs.jsonl](evidence/differential-inputs.jsonl),
+[differential-mismatches.jsonl](evidence/differential-mismatches.jsonl),
+[differential-summary.json](evidence/differential-summary.json), and
+[differential.log](evidence/differential.log). This is finite implementation
+evidence, not a substitute for the K proof.
+
+## 3. Clean proof reconstruction
+
+The live toolchain was K v7.1.337; exact binaries and versions are recorded in
+[toolchain.log](evidence/toolchain.log).
+
+Fresh source builds were performed with:
+
+```text
+kompile reference-semantics/semantics.k --backend llvm \
+  --main-module MPY-KRUN --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \
+  --output-definition runtime-kompiled
+
+kompile verification.k --backend haskell \
+  --main-module PROD-SIGNS-VERIFICATION --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \
+  --output-definition verification-kompiled
+```
+
